nodes.title: A complete elliptic 2-descent
nodes.statement: For E : y² = x³ − x over ℚ (S = {2, ∞}): E[2](ℚ) = {O, (0,0), (±1, 0)}; the local images at 2 and ∞ and the unramified conditions elsewhere cut Sel²(E/ℚ) ⊆ H¹(G_{ℚ,S}, E[2]) down to the image of E[2](ℚ), so Sel²(E/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/2)², Ш(E/ℚ)[2] = 0, rank E(ℚ) = 0 and E(ℚ) = E[2](ℚ) is finitely generated. The Selmer bound is only an upper bound: for the Jacobian of an everywhere locally soluble genus-one curve y² = f(x) with no rational point (Bhargava–Gross–Wang Theorem 10, g = 1), W[2] is a Selmer element outside the Kummer image, so #Sel² > #E(ℚ)/2E(ℚ).
hypotheses: ℚ, S = {2, ∞}; the x − T descent map of Tau Ceti identifies H¹(ℚ, E[2]) with the kernel of the norm on (ℚ^× /ℚ^{×2})³.
proofSteps: Compute the image of the descent map on E[2](ℚ); compute local images at 2 and ∞; intersect (EllipticCurves Layer 6 explicit 2-descent, already formalised in Tau Ceti's Stoll development).
Apply descent-sequence and mordell-weil.
acceptance: rank E(ℚ) = 0 and #E(ℚ) = 4.

sources.match: The explicit 2-Selmer group in the étale algebra, its finiteness, and the rank bound.

nodes.title: Formal logarithms on a sufficiently small ideal
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite, O its integers, 𝔪 its maximal ideal, and e=ord_F(p). For a g-dimensional commutative formal group law over O, represented by g native multivariate power series with zero constant term, linear term X+Y, associativity, identity and inverses, there is a unique formal logarithm log_FG over F with derivative the identity. For every integer r>e/(p−1), it converges on (𝔪^r)^g and gives an analytic group isomorphism FG((𝔪^r)^g)≃((𝔪^r)^g,+), with analytic inverse and the same tangent map. In particular the whole maximal-ideal group is torsion-free when e<p−1. This is a multivariate logarithm theorem extending native one-dimensional FormalGroup; native FormalGroup.Point is a power-series-valued point type and does not already give points in a complete local field.
hypotheses: The formal law has integral coefficients and is commutative; F has characteristic zero; use ord_F(π)=1 and r∈ℕ with r>e/(p−1).

A smooth group model at the identity supplies its formal law and comparison with the kernel of reduction; that comparison is a separate NeronModels supplier contract. For an abelian variety without good reduction one still uses the smooth Néron model near the identity.
proofSteps: The inverse Jacobian in the second variables at Y=0 gives the g invariant differential forms with integral coefficients and identity constant matrix. Commutativity makes them closed. Integrate their homogeneous degree-(n−1) parts over F to obtain the degree-n part of log, whose denominators divide n. Translation invariance gives log(FG(X,Y))=log(X)+log(Y); derivative identity determines uniqueness in characteristic zero.

A homogeneous degree-n coefficient has valuation at least −e·ord_p(n). Since ord_p(n)≤(n−1)/(p−1), on 𝔪^r the nonlinear term has valuation at least nr−e·ord_p(n)>r and tends to infinity with n. The same estimates on differences show log−id is strictly contracting on (𝔪^r)^g. Solve log(x)=y by iterating x↦y−(log(x)−x); completeness gives its inverse on the whole ball. The power-series inverse is analytic by the same estimates. Log is a homomorphism, hence the inverse is too.

Katz Appendix Lemma′ proves the r=1 range by topologically nilpotent divided powers on 𝔪, followed by inverse logarithm and exponential; the coefficient proof gives the explicit small-ball refinement used here. The target is the logarithm, not a redevelopment of general Lie groups or an elliptic formal-group carrier.
acceptance: For the additive g-dimensional law log is the identity on every ideal.
For the multiplicative law in one variable log(1+T)=Σ_{n≥1}(−1)^{n+1}T^n/n and its inverse exp(T)−1 satisfy the stated strict-radius condition.
At F=ℚ_p(ζ_p), e=p−1 and ζ_p−1∈𝔪 is nonzero p-torsion for the multiplicative law. At p=2 the witness is −2 over ℚ₂. Thus the strict inequality for r=1 cannot be replaced by e≤p−1.

sources.locator: Appendix, Lemma′ and its proof, printed p.502 (the Appendix begins on p.501)
sources.match: Primary proof of logarithm/exponential isomorphism and torsion-freeness for e<p−1; the explicit r bound is the stated coefficient-estimate refinement.
Analytic additive coordinates near the identity, with identity tangent normalization and linear change between charts.

nodes.title: Local indices of multiplication by two
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety of dimension g over F/ℚ_p finite. Mattuck gives an open finite-index subgroup U≃(O_F^g,+) of A(F). With the module absolute value |a|_F=q_F^(−ord_F(a)), #A(F)/2A(F)=|2|_F^(−g)·#A(F)[2]. Thus the factor is 2^(g[F:ℚ₂]) at p=2 and 1 otherwise; for F=ℚ₂ and full two-torsion it gives 2^(3g). This module absolute value is not the extension of the normalized ℚ_p norm without its [F:ℚ_p] power. Over ℝ the quotient has order #A(ℝ)[2]/2^g; over ℂ it is trivial.
hypotheses: A abelian of dimension g over a local field of characteristic 0.
proofSteps: Read Mattuck Theorem 7, pp.114–117: its additive local uniformization sends an abelian subgroup into a linear subspace; projective compactness over a locally compact F makes the open subgroup finite index. An alternative implementation uses a smooth Néron identity chart, shrinks and rescales it until its formal law is integral, and applies formal-logarithm-small-ball. The model/chart comparison is an explicit supplier request, not an existing abelian-variety logarithm at the pins.

Let G=A(F), C=G/U. Since U is torsion-free, multiplication by two in 0→U→G→C→0 gives 0→G[2]→C[2]→U/2U→G/2G→C/2C→0. Both C groups are finite with equal order. Taking alternating cardinalities gives #G/2G=#G[2]·#U/2U, without assuming this group extension splits. For U≃O_F^g the last factor is q_F^(g ord_F(2))=|2|_F^(−g).

Over ℂ import complex-lattice-realization: A(ℂ)≃ℂ^g/Λ, where multiplication by two is surjective. Over ℝ take conjugation invariants in that uniformization. The identity component is a real g-torus; the component group embeds in H¹(⟨conjugation⟩,Λ), hence is killed by two. In 0→G⁰→G→π₀G→0, [2] is onto on G⁰ and G⁰[2] has order 2^g. The snake lemma gives G[2]↠π₀G and G/2G≃π₀G, proving the stated real count. No splitting hypothesis is needed.
acceptance: For E/ℚ₂ with E(ℚ₂)[2] = ℤ/2 × ℤ/2, #E(ℚ₂)/2E(ℚ₂) = 8.
If F/ℚ₂ is unramified quadratic and g=1 with all four two-torsion points rational, the quotient has order 4·4=16, not 8.
At p odd the additive lattice contributes no two-quotient. For g=0 both sides equal 1.
A real elliptic curve with one component has #E(ℝ)[2]=2 and quotient order 1; with two components these orders are 4 and 2. A complex abelian variety has quotient order 1.

sources.locator: §13, Theorem 7 and proof, printed pp.114–117; §14(2), p.118
sources.match: Primary proof of an additive open subgroup, finite index for locally compact fields. The index is then obtained by the displayed finite-group exact sequence.

nodes.title: Reduction is injective on torsion
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field K with good reduction at a finite place v of residue characteristic p, absolute ramification index e_v, and 𝒜 the abelian scheme over O_v. The reduction map A(K_v)_tors → 𝒜(k_v) is injective on torsion of order prime to p, and on all torsion if e_v < p − 1. For the Jacobian J of a curve C over ℚ with good reduction at q, the reduction J(ℚ) → J̃(𝔽_q) is a homomorphism compatible with reduction of points and divisors, injective on torsion for q ≥ 3.
hypotheses: Good reduction at v; e_v < p − 1 for the p-part.
proofSteps: Properness identifies A(F) with 𝒜(O_F) at a good-reduction place. The smooth formal completion of 𝒜 at zero identifies ker(red) with its g-dimensional integral commutative formal law on 𝔪_F; this comparison is requested explicitly from NeronModels R11.1.

For n prime to p, [n](T)=nT+higher-degree terms on the formal completion. On 𝔪_F the linear term is a unit and the nonlinear terms strictly contract, so [n] is bijective there by successive approximation; in particular the kernel has no prime-to-p torsion. Étaleness alone is not asserted to make all global n-torsion trivial.

If e_v<p−1, formal-logarithm-small-ball applies with r=1 and identifies the full reduction kernel with the torsion-free additive group 𝔪_F^g. This is precisely Katz Appendix Lemma′ and its logarithm/exponential proof on printed p.502. Consequently all torsion injects under the strict ramification bound.
Base change of the Jacobian and its Abel–Jacobi map to the good-reduction model gives compatibility with points and divisor classes; restrict the local statement to J(ℚ). At q≥3 one has e=1<q−1.
acceptance: E : y² = x³ − x has good reduction at 3 and E(ℚ)_tors = ℤ/2 × ℤ/2 injects into Ẽ(𝔽₃), of order 4.

On the multiplicative formal group over ℚ_p(ζ_p), e=p−1 and ζ_p−1 is nonzero p-torsion in the reduction kernel: the strict boundary cannot be weakened, nor can the restriction to prime-to-p torsion be dropped without a ramification hypothesis.
For a dimension-zero abelian variety both torsion and reduction groups are trivial.

sources.locator: Appendix, Lemma and Lemma′, printed p.502; setup on p.501
sources.match: Katz proves the local kernel torsion-free using logarithm and exponential when e<p−1, and derives the global torsion reduction injection.

sources.locator: §6.5, Theorem 6.5.13 proof, Step 2 (Lang and Hensel), p. 184
sources.match: Hensel lifting along smooth group schemes over complete DVRs.

nodes.title: The Kummer map of a two-isogeny
nodes.statement: For E : y² = x(x² + cx + d) over ℚ with d(c² − 4d) ≠ 0, the 2-isogeny φ : E → E' with E' : y² = x(x² − 2cx + c² − 4d) and its dual φ' : E' → E: the Kummer map E(ℚ)/φ'(E'(ℚ)) → H¹(ℚ, E'[φ']) ≅ ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} is (x, y) ↦ x for x ≠ 0, (0, 0) ↦ d, O ↦ 1; the φ'-Selmer group is the set of d₁ ∈ ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} dividing d up to squares for which v² = d₁u⁴ + cu² + d/d₁ is everywhere locally soluble; its quotient by the image of E(ℚ) is Ш(E'/ℚ)[φ'].
hypotheses: E with a rational 2-torsion point at (0, 0); characteristic 0.

Use an integral Weierstrass normalization for c,d and S containing primes dividing 2d and the bad-reduction set. Test local solubility on the smooth projective model of the homogeneous quartic, including points at infinity.
proofSteps: Instance of kummer-map for the degree-two isogeny: E'[φ'] ≅ μ₂ and H¹(ℚ, μ₂) ≅ ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2} (Kummer theory); the fibre of φ' over (x, y) is the quadratic extension ℚ(√x).
Selmer condition: everywhere local solubility of the homogeneous spaces v² = d₁u⁴ + cu² + d/d₁ (descent-sequence).
The divisor bound for square classes uses the integral equation. Local solubility is not restricted to the displayed affine chart of the covering.
acceptance: For E : y² = x³ − x (c = 0, d = −1), the image of E(ℚ) is {1, −1} ⊆ ℚ^×/ℚ^{×2}.

sources.match: Selmer groups of isogenies as Selmer sets of the isogeny torsor.

sources.match: Isogeny Selmer groups of elliptic curves with their Kummer sequences.

nodes.title: The topology on points with values in a topological algebra
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, A a commutative R-algebra and B a commutative topological ring which is an R-algebra. The B-valued points of Spec A are Points_R(A, B) := A →ₐ[R] B. The points topology on Points_R(A, B) is the topology induced by the injection Points_R(A, B) → B^A, φ ↦ (φ(a))_{a ∈ A}, where B^A = (A → B) carries the product topology; equivalently, it is the coarsest topology for which every evaluation φ ↦ φ(a), a ∈ A, is continuous. Lean: `TauCeti.Points R A B`, a type synonym of `A →ₐ[R] B` carrying this topology as an instance; no topology instance is put on `A →ₐ[R] B` itself, so no existing instance is overridden.
hypotheses: R and A commutative; B a commutative topological ring with an R-algebra structure. No finiteness of A and no separation axiom on B is assumed in the definition; the separation, closedness and local-compactness statements of RP.2/points-topology-presentation assume them.
proofSteps: Define the topology as TopologicalSpace.induced along the coercion Points_R(A, B) → (A → B), with Pi.topologicalSpace on the target. The coercion is injective (algebra maps are determined by their values), so this is the subspace topology of the image.
Continuity into Points: a map f from a topological space Z is continuous iff every z ↦ f(z)(a) is continuous (induced topology and product topology universal properties).

Functoriality: for g : A′ →ₐ[R] A, φ ↦ φ ∘ g is continuous, because each evaluation of the composite at a′ is the evaluation at g(a′). For a continuous R-algebra map h : B → B′, φ ↦ h ∘ φ is continuous, because each evaluation of the composite is h composed with an evaluation.

Products: Algebra.TensorProduct.liftEquiv identifies Points_R(A ⊗_R A′, B) with pairs (φ, φ′) (the commutation condition is automatic since B is commutative). The map φ ↦ (φ ∘ includeLeft, φ ∘ includeRight) is continuous by functoriality, and its inverse is continuous because each element of A ⊗_R A′ is a finite sum of products a ⊗ a′, whose value (φ(a)φ′(a′) summed) is a continuous function of (φ, φ′) as B is a topological ring.

Examples: for A = R[X], Polynomial.aeval identifies Points_R(R[X], B) with B through φ ↦ φ(X), a homeomorphism since every evaluation is a polynomial function of φ(X). For A = R[X, Y]/(XY − 1), φ ↦ φ(X) is a bijection onto Bˣ, and the points topology corresponds to Mathlib's topology on units (induced by u ↦ (u, u⁻¹), Units.embedProduct), because the points topology is induced by the two evaluations at X and Y = X⁻¹.
acceptance: Every evaluation map is continuous, and a map into Points is continuous iff all its evaluations are.

For A = R[X, Y]/(XY − 1) and B = 𝔸_ℚ, the space is 𝔸_ℚˣ with the topology in which u and u⁻¹ both vary continuously; it is not the subspace topology from 𝔸_ℚ (Conrad §3). A definition through the embedding of Spec A in the affine line would get this wrong.
No presentation of A enters the definition; that any presentation gives the same topology is a lemma (RP.2/points-topology-presentation).

sources.match: Conrad's topological ring R is the value ring B here; his explicit description of the topology is taken as the definition.
The units example of the acceptance cases.

nodes.title: Presentations compute the points topology
nodes.statement: Let R, A, B be as in RP.2/points-topology, n ∈ ℕ and π : R[X₁, …, X_n] → A a surjective R-algebra map (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R), with aᵢ := π(Xᵢ). Then φ ↦ (φ(a₁), …, φ(a_n)) is a topological embedding Points_R(A, B) → Bⁿ whose image is Z(ker π) := {b ∈ Bⁿ : aeval b f = 0 for all f ∈ ker π}. If B is T1, Z(ker π) is closed, so the embedding is closed and Points_R(A, B) is T1; if B is Hausdorff, Points_R(A, B) is Hausdorff; if B is locally compact Hausdorff, Points_R(A, B) is locally compact.
hypotheses: π surjective; for the closedness statements B is T1 (resp. Hausdorff, locally compact Hausdorff).
proofSteps: Bijection onto Z(ker π): an R-algebra map out of the quotient A ≅ R[X]/ker π is determined by the images of the Xᵢ, and b ∈ Bⁿ is the image of such a map iff MvPolynomial.aeval b kills ker π.

Embedding: the map is continuous (n evaluations). Conversely every a ∈ A is π(f) for a polynomial f, and φ(a) = aeval (φ(a₁), …, φ(a_n)) f is a polynomial function of the coordinates, continuous because B is a topological ring; so each evaluation factors continuously through the image, and the points topology is induced from Bⁿ.
Closedness: Z(ker π) = ⋂_{f ∈ ker π} (b ↦ aeval b f)⁻¹{0}, an intersection of closed sets when {0} is closed.
Separation and local compactness pass to subspaces, and closed subspaces of locally compact Hausdorff spaces are locally compact.
acceptance: For A = R[X]/(X² − 2) and B = ℝ, the image is {±√2} ⊂ ℝ, a closed two-point set.
Two presentations of A give homeomorphic zero sets; the homeomorphism is given by polynomial maps in both directions.

sources.match: Independence of the presentation, which the proof deduces from the polynomial expression of every element in the generators.
Closedness of the image and local compactness.

api.name: TauCeti.Points.isEmbedding_generators
api.statement: For a surjection π from MvPolynomial (Fin n) R onto A, the evaluation at π(X₁), …, π(X_n) is a topological embedding Points_R(A, B) → Fin n → B.

nodes.title: Changing the value ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a finitely generated R-algebra and h : B → B′ a continuous R-algebra map of commutative topological R-algebras. Then postcomposition Points_R(A, B) → Points_R(A, B′) is continuous. If h is a topological embedding, so is the induced map; if h is moreover a closed (resp. open) embedding, so is the induced map; and if h(B) is discrete in B′, the image of Points_R(A, B) is discrete in Points_R(A, B′).
hypotheses: A finitely generated; h continuous. The source's closed/open clause is stated with the roles of the two rings exchanged (sourceIssues HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions/E8); the statement here uses the corrected orientation.
proofSteps: Choose a presentation π : R[X₁, …, X_n] → A (A finitely generated). By RP.2/points-topology-presentation both Points spaces embed in Bⁿ and B′ⁿ as the zero sets of ker π, and the induced map is the restriction of hⁿ : Bⁿ → B′ⁿ, since h is an algebra map.

If h is an embedding (resp. closed, open embedding), so is hⁿ, and Points_R(A, B) = hⁿ⁻¹(Points_R(A, B′)) inside Bⁿ, because a tuple satisfies the equations of ker π in B iff its image does in B′ (h injective). Restrictions of (closed, open) embeddings to preimages are (closed, open) embeddings.
Discreteness: hⁿ(Bⁿ) is discrete in B′ⁿ when h(B) is discrete in B′ (finite products of discrete subspaces), and the image of Points_R(A, B) is a subset of it.
acceptance: The inclusion K → 𝔸_K of a number field into its adele ring gives a discrete embedding of the K-points of any affine K-variety into its adelic points (RP.2/rational-points-discrete).
The inclusion of the valuation ring O_v into K_v is an open and closed embedding, so the integral points of an O_v-model are open and closed in the K_v-points.

sources.match: The discreteness clause, stated in the correct orientation in the source.
The closed and open clauses; the printed hypothesis 'R′ closed in R' has the two rings exchanged (sourceIssues E8).

nodes.title: Adelic points of an affine variety
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, 𝔸_K = NumberField.AdeleRing (𝓞 K) K its adele ring (the product of the infinite adele ring and the finite adele ring), and A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra, the coordinate ring of the affine K-variety X = Spec A. The adelic points of X are X(𝔸_K) := Points_K(A, 𝔸_K) with the points topology (RP.2/points-topology). They come with: the diagonal ι : X(K) = Points_K(A, K) → X(𝔸_K), postcomposition with the algebra map K → 𝔸_K; for each finite place v (a height-one prime of 𝓞 K) the local projection X(𝔸_K) → X(K_v), K_v = v.adicCompletion K, postcomposition with the projection of the finite adeles to their v-component; and for each infinite place w the local projection X(𝔸_K) → X(K_w), K_w = w.Completion. All of these are continuous. Lean: `TauCeti.AdelicPoints K A`, with `diagonal`, `finiteProj v` and `infiniteProj w`.
hypotheses: K a number field; A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra (so X is an affine K-scheme of finite type). Non-affine varieties are not covered by this node (coverage).
proofSteps: Definition: Points_K(A, 𝔸_K). The adele ring is a topological K-algebra (NumberField.AdeleRing is a topological ring with Algebra K).

Diagonal and projections: the algebra map K → 𝔸_K and the projections 𝔸_K → K_v are continuous K-algebra maps (the projection of the finite adeles to a component is RestrictedProduct.evalRingHom, continuous for the restricted-product topology; the infinite part is a product of the K_w). Postcomposition is continuous by RP.2/points-topology.

Product decomposition: since 𝔸_K = K_∞ × 𝔸_K^f, Points_K(A, 𝔸_K) ≃ₜ Points_K(A, K_∞) × Points_K(A, 𝔸_K^f) and Points_K(A, K_∞) ≃ₜ ∏_w X(K_w) (algebra maps into a product are families of algebra maps into the factors; the topologies agree because both are induced by the evaluations).

Hausdorff: 𝔸_K is Hausdorff (Tau Ceti NumberField.AdeleRing.instT2Space), so RP.2/points-topology-presentation makes X(𝔸_K) Hausdorff. Local compactness: the infinite adeles are locally compact (NumberField.InfiniteAdeleRing.locallyCompactSpace), and the finite adeles are locally compact by RestrictedProduct.locallyCompactSpace_of_group once each O_v is compact; compactness of O_v for a number field is not in the pinned libraries (gap), so the local-compactness API item waits for it.
acceptance: X(𝔸_K) is Hausdorff, and X(K) sits in it as a discrete closed subset (RP.2/rational-points-discrete).
For K = ℚ and A = ℚ[X]/(X² + 1), X(𝔸_ℚ) is empty although X(ℚ_p) is nonempty for every p ≡ 1 mod 4, because X(ℝ) is empty.

sources.match: Adelic points as the A-points of X for the adele ring A of the global field k.

nodes.title: Integral models and their integral local points
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra. An integral model of A is a finitely generated 𝓞_K-subalgebra A₀ ⊆ A such that K·A₀ = A (equivalently, the K-subalgebra generated by A₀ is A; then A₀ ⊗_{𝓞_K} K ≅ A). For a finite place v, its integral points at v are X₀(O_v) := {x ∈ X(K_v) : x(A₀) ⊆ O_v}, where O_v = v.adicCompletionIntegers K; for an infinite place w, X₀(O_w) := X(K_w). Lean: `TauCeti.AdelicPoints.IntegralModel K A` (a structure holding A₀, finite generation and the spanning condition) with `IntegralModel.integralPoints`.
hypotheses: K a number field; A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra; A₀ a finitely generated 𝓞_K-subalgebra with K·A₀ = A. Models over rings of S-integers are the localisations A₀[1/N]; since the restricted product only sees almost all places, 𝓞_K-models suffice.
proofSteps: A₀ is torsion free over 𝓞_K (a subring of the K-vector space A), so A₀ ⊗_{𝓞_K} K is the localisation of A₀ at 𝓞_K ∖ {0}, which is K·A₀ = A.
A K-algebra map x : A → K_v is determined by its restriction to A₀, and x ∈ X₀(O_v) iff that restriction lands in O_v; so X₀(O_v) is identified with the 𝓞_K-algebra maps A₀ → O_v.
If a₁, …, a_n generate A₀ over 𝓞_K, then X₀(O_v) = {x : x(aᵢ) ∈ O_v for all i}, because O_v is a subring containing the image of 𝓞_K.

For an arbitrary affine finite-type scheme, prove compactness of integral points through a finite presentation as a closed locus in O_v^n. RestrictedProduct.locallyCompactSpace_of_group supplies the ambient adelic group only; X(K_v) is generally not a group.
acceptance: For A = ℚ[X] and A₀ = ℤ[X], X₀(ℤ_p) is ℤ_p inside ℚ_p.
Different models may differ at finitely many places: for A = ℚ[X], A₀ = ℤ[X] and A₀′ = ℤ[X/2] have X₀(ℤ₂) = ℤ₂ ≠ 2ℤ₂ = X₀′(ℤ₂), and agree at every odd p (RP.2/integral-model-exists-unique).

nodes.title: Integral models exist and agree at almost all places
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra. (a) The 𝓞_K-subalgebra generated by any finite family of K-algebra generators of A is an integral model (RP.2/integral-model). (b) For two integral models A₀, A₀′ there is a nonzero N ∈ 𝓞_K with A₀[1/N] = A₀′[1/N] inside A; consequently X₀(O_v) = X₀′(O_v) for every finite place v not dividing N, i.e. for all but finitely many v.
hypotheses: A finitely generated over K; A₀, A₀′ finitely generated 𝓞_K-subalgebras spanning A over K.
proofSteps: (a) The subalgebra generated by K-algebra generators a₁, …, a_n is finitely generated over 𝓞_K, and its K-span contains the aᵢ and is a K-subalgebra, hence is A.

(b) Each of the finitely many generators of A₀′ lies in A = K·A₀, so it is a/m with a ∈ A₀ and m ∈ 𝓞_K ∖ {0}; let N₁ be the product of these denominators, so A₀′ ⊆ A₀[1/N₁]. Symmetrically A₀ ⊆ A₀′[1/N₂]. With N = N₁N₂, A₀[1/N] = A₀′[1/N].
If v does not divide N, N is a unit of O_v, so a K-algebra map x : A → K_v with x(A₀) ⊆ O_v also sends A₀[1/N], hence A₀′, into O_v, and conversely.
Only finitely many height-one primes contain N ≠ 0 (a nonzero element of a Dedekind domain lies in finitely many maximal ideals).
acceptance: The models ℤ[X] and ℤ[X/2] of ℚ[X] satisfy (b) with N = 2.

sources.match: Uniqueness of spreading out, specialised to affine models over the rings 𝓞_K[1/N] whose limit is K.
The denominator-chasing argument in the affine case.

nodes.title: Adelic points as a restricted product
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra and A₀ an integral model (RP.2/integral-model). Then the local projections give a homeomorphism X(𝔸_K) ≃ₜ (∏_{w infinite} X(K_w)) × Πʳ_{v finite} [X(K_v), X₀(O_v)], where the second factor is Mathlib's restricted product of the X(K_v) with respect to the subsets X₀(O_v) (RestrictedProduct, with its restricted-product topology). In particular an element of X(𝔸_K) is exactly a family (x_v) of local points with x_v ∈ X₀(O_v) for all but finitely many finite v, and the restricted product does not depend on the model (RP.2/integral-model-exists-unique).
hypotheses: K a number field; A finitely generated; A₀ an integral model. The infinite places are finitely many, so their factor is an ordinary product.
proofSteps: Product decomposition: RP.2/adelic-points reduces the statement to the finite adeles 𝔸_K^f = Πʳ_v [K_v, O_v].

Bijection: let a₁, …, a_n generate A₀ over 𝓞_K (they then generate A over K). For a K-algebra map φ : A → 𝔸_K^f, each φ(aᵢ) is a finite adele, so it lies in O_v for all v outside a finite set Tᵢ (RestrictedProduct.eventually); for v outside T = ⋃ Tᵢ the v-component x_v of φ sends every aᵢ, hence A₀, into O_v. Conversely a family (x_v) with x_v(A₀) ⊆ O_v for almost all v defines a family of adeles (x_v(a))_v for each a ∈ A (a = b/m with b ∈ A₀, and m is a unit at almost all v), and a K-algebra map into the restricted product, because ring operations in the restricted product are componentwise.

Topology: by RP.2/points-topology-presentation both sides embed as the zero set of the same ideal, the left side in (𝔸_K^f)ⁿ and the right side in Πʳ_v [K_vⁿ, O_vⁿ], through the values at a₁, …, a_n; and (𝔸_K^f)ⁿ = Πʳ_v [K_vⁿ, O_vⁿ] as topological rings (a finite product of restricted products is the restricted product of the products; open O_v). Under this identification the two embeddings agree, so the bijection is a homeomorphism.

Openness of the X₀(O_v): they are cut out by the open conditions x(aᵢ) ∈ O_v (RP.2/integral-model), which is what makes the restricted-product topology the right one (RestrictedProduct.isOpen_forall_mem).
Model independence: two models have the same integral points at almost all v, and a restricted product only depends on the subsets at almost all indices.
acceptance: For A = K[X], the theorem is Mathlib's definition of the finite adele ring as Πʳ_v [K_v, O_v] (with the model 𝓞_K[X]).

For A = K[X, Y]/(XY − 1) with model 𝓞_K[X, Y]/(XY − 1), it describes the idele group as the restricted product of the K_vˣ with respect to the O_vˣ, as groups and topologically; this agrees with Mathlib's unitsEquiv as groups.

The bijection with the restricted product of local points.
Conrad's theorem: the S-integral adelic points are the product of local points, homeomorphically in the affine case; passing to the limit over S gives the restricted product.

nodes.title: Adelic points exist iff local points exist and are integral almost everywhere
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra and A₀ an integral model. Then X(𝔸_K) is nonempty iff X(K_w) is nonempty for every infinite place w, X(K_v) is nonempty for every finite place v, and X₀(O_v) is nonempty for all but finitely many finite v. In particular X(K) ≠ ∅ implies X(𝔸_K) ≠ ∅ (through the diagonal), and X(𝔸_K) = ∅ as soon as X has no point over a single completion.
hypotheses: As in RP.2/adelic-points-restricted-product.
proofSteps: By RP.2/adelic-points-restricted-product, an adelic point is a family of local points integral at almost all v; such a family exists iff every local set is nonempty and the integral subsets are nonempty at almost all v (choose integral points there and arbitrary points at the finitely many remaining places).
The diagonal image of a K-point is an adelic point (RP.2/adelic-points).
acceptance: For A = ℚ[X]/(X² + 1): X(ℝ) = ∅, so X(𝔸_ℚ) = ∅.
Local points must exist at every place: for A = ℚ[X]/(X² − 2), X(ℚ_p) is empty for every p ≡ ±3 mod 8, so X(𝔸_ℚ) = ∅ although X(ℝ) ≠ ∅.
The lemma says nothing about X(K): the Brauer–Manin set (RP.2/brauer-manin-pairing) refines this necessary condition.

sources.match: Nonemptiness of X(𝔸) is the local condition that the obstructions refine.

nodes.title: Rational points are discrete and closed in adelic points
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra. The diagonal ι : X(K) → X(𝔸_K) is injective, and its image is a discrete closed subset of X(𝔸_K).
hypotheses: K a number field; A finitely generated.
proofSteps: Choose a presentation of A. By RP.2/points-topology-presentation, X(𝔸_K) embeds as a closed subset of 𝔸_Kⁿ, compatibly with the embedding X(K) ⊆ Kⁿ, and ι is the restriction of the diagonal Kⁿ → 𝔸_Kⁿ.

K is discrete and closed in 𝔸_K (Tau Ceti discreteTopology_principalSubgroup, isClosed_principalSubgroup), so Kⁿ is discrete and closed in 𝔸_Kⁿ, and its intersection with X(𝔸_K) is the image of ι (a tuple in Kⁿ satisfies the equations in 𝔸_K iff it satisfies them in K, since K → 𝔸_K is injective).
Discreteness also follows from RP.2/points-topology-base-change.
acceptance: For A = K[X], the image of ι is the principal subgroup K ⊆ 𝔸_K.

sources.match: Discreteness of the rational points in the adelic points.

nodes.title: Base change of Azumaya algebras
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, 𝒜 an Azumaya R-algebra (Mathlib IsAzumaya R 𝒜: finitely generated, projective and faithful as an R-module, with R-algebra map 𝒜 ⊗_R 𝒜ᵐᵒᵖ → End_R(𝒜) bijective), and S a commutative R-algebra. Then S ⊗_R 𝒜 is an Azumaya S-algebra. Over a field L, 𝒜 is Azumaya iff 𝒜 is a nonzero finite-dimensional central simple L-algebra.
hypotheses: R, S commutative; 𝒜 Azumaya over R. For the field statement, L is a field.
proofSteps: Module conditions: S ⊗_R 𝒜 is finitely generated and projective over S (base change of finite projective modules). Faithfulness: a finite projective faithful module has positive rank at every prime of R, and base change preserves positive rank at primes of S, so S ⊗_R 𝒜 is faithful.

The algebra map: S ⊗_R (𝒜 ⊗_R 𝒜ᵐᵒᵖ) ≅ (S ⊗_R 𝒜) ⊗_S (S ⊗_R 𝒜)ᵐᵒᵖ, and, since 𝒜 is finite projective, S ⊗_R End_R(𝒜) ≅ End_S(S ⊗_R 𝒜); under these isomorphisms the map for S ⊗_R 𝒜 is the base change of the bijective map for 𝒜.

Field case: over a field, Azumaya algebras are free, and Mathlib's instance Algebra.IsCentral.instIsAzumaya gives centrality. Simplicity: a two-sided ideal I of 𝒜 gives a two-sided ideal I ⊗ 𝒜ᵐᵒᵖ of 𝒜 ⊗ 𝒜ᵐᵒᵖ ≅ End_L(𝒜), which is simple, so I = 0 or I = 𝒜. Conversely a finite-dimensional central simple algebra is Azumaya (Tau Ceti IsSimpleRing.isAzumaya).
Consequently S ⊗_R 𝒜 over a field S = L is a central simple L-algebra; this is what makes Brauer evaluation (RP.2/brauer-evaluation) land in Mathlib's Brauer group of L.
acceptance: The matrix algebra M_n(R) is Azumaya (IsAzumaya.matrix) and its base change is M_n(S).
The Hamilton quaternions over ℤ[1/2] form an Azumaya algebra; their base change to ℝ is ℍ, central simple and not split.

sources.match: Azumaya algebras as locally free algebras with 𝒜 ⊗ 𝒜ᵒᵖ ≅ End(𝒜), the form Mathlib's IsAzumaya takes on affine schemes; stability under base change is built into the local characterisations of Definition 6.6.12.
Over a field, Azumaya algebras are the central simple algebras.

nodes.title: Evaluating an Azumaya algebra at a point
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, A a commutative K-algebra, 𝒜 an Azumaya A-algebra and L a field with a K-algebra structure. For x ∈ Points_K(A, L), the evaluation of 𝒜 at x is 𝒜(x) := [L ⊗_{A, x} 𝒜] ∈ Br(L), the Brauer class (Tau Ceti BrauerGroup.mk of CSA.of) of the central simple L-algebra obtained by base change along x (RP.2/azumaya-base-change). Properties: (a) naturality: for a field extension L → L′ compatible with the K-structures, 𝒜(x′) = baseChange_{L′/L}(𝒜(x)) for x′ the composite point (Tau Ceti BrauerGroup.baseChange); (b) multiplicativity: (𝒜 ⊗_A 𝒜′)(x) = 𝒜(x)·𝒜′(x), 𝒜ᵐᵒᵖ(x) = 𝒜(x)⁻¹, and End_A(P)(x) = 1 for a finite projective A-module P of positive rank; (c) pullback: for a K-algebra map g : A′ → A (so A is an A′-algebra) and an Azumaya A′-algebra 𝒜′, (A ⊗_{A′} 𝒜′)(x) = 𝒜′(x ∘ g); (d) constant algebras: for a central simple K-algebra D, (A ⊗_K D)(x) = baseChange_{L/K}[D]. Lean: `TauCeti.BrauerManin.eval 𝒜 x : BrauerGroup L`.
hypotheses: K, L fields, L a K-algebra; A commutative; 𝒜 Azumaya over A. All types in one universe, as Tau Ceti's BrauerGroup group structure requires.
proofSteps: Well-defined: L ⊗_{A,x} 𝒜 is Azumaya over L by RP.2/azumaya-base-change, hence central simple and finite-dimensional, so CSA.of applies.
(a) L′ ⊗_L (L ⊗_{A,x} 𝒜) ≅ L′ ⊗_{A,x′} 𝒜 (associativity of base change), and Tau Ceti BrauerGroup.baseChange_mk computes the class of the left side.

(b) L ⊗_A (𝒜 ⊗_A 𝒜′) ≅ (L ⊗_A 𝒜) ⊗_L (L ⊗_A 𝒜′) and L ⊗_A 𝒜ᵐᵒᵖ ≅ (L ⊗_A 𝒜)ᵐᵒᵖ; Tau Ceti mk_tensorProduct and mk_op. L ⊗_A End_A(P) ≅ End_L(L ⊗_A P) with L ⊗_A P a nonzero finite-dimensional L-vector space; Tau Ceti mk_end.
(c), (d): associativity of base change, L ⊗_{A,x} (A ⊗_{A′} 𝒜′) ≅ L ⊗_{A′, x∘g} 𝒜′ and L ⊗_A (A ⊗_K D) ≅ L ⊗_K D.
acceptance: The trivial algebra 𝒜 = A and matrix algebras evaluate to 1 at every point.

Evaluation genuinely depends on the point: for K = ℚ, A = ℚ[t, 1/t] and the quaternion algebra 𝒜 = (−1, t)_A, 𝒜 evaluated at t = 1 in ℝ is split, and at t = −1 in ℝ it is the class of ℍ, the nontrivial element of Br(ℝ).

sources.match: Evaluation of a Brauer class at an L-point by pullback; for Azumaya algebras the pullback is the base change along the point.
The group law on Azumaya classes that evaluation respects.

nodes.title: Spreading out an Azumaya algebra over an integral model
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra with integral model A₀ (RP.2/integral-model), and 𝒜 an Azumaya A-algebra. Then there are a nonzero N ∈ 𝓞_K and an Azumaya A₀[1/N]-algebra 𝒜₀ with A ⊗_{A₀[1/N]} 𝒜₀ ≅ 𝒜 as A-algebras.
hypotheses: A = A₀ ⊗_{𝓞_K} K is the filtered colimit of the rings A₀[1/N], N ∈ 𝓞_K ∖ {0}.
proofSteps: 𝒜 is finitely presented as an A-module (finite projective) and as an A-algebra; choose a finite presentation of the module and of the multiplication table. Its finitely many coefficients lie in A₀[1/N] for some N, giving an A₀[1/N]-algebra 𝒜₀ with A ⊗ 𝒜₀ ≅ 𝒜 (descent of finitely presented objects to a stage of a filtered colimit).

Projectivity: a finitely presented module whose base change to the colimit is projective is projective after enlarging N (a projective module is a direct summand of a free one; the splitting is a finite amount of data and descends).

Bijectivity of 𝒜₀ ⊗ 𝒜₀ᵐᵒᵖ → End(𝒜₀): a map of finite projective modules which becomes bijective over the colimit is bijective after enlarging N (its inverse and the two composite identities are finitely many equations). Faithfulness: positive rank at every prime holds after enlarging N, since the rank function is locally constant and positive on A.
This is the Azumaya form of Poonen's Corollary 6.6.11 (spreading out a Brauer class), which Poonen proves for cohomological Brauer classes through the limit theorem for étale cohomology.
acceptance: A constant algebra A ⊗_K D with D central simple over K spreads out over A₀[1/N] as A₀[1/N] ⊗ D₀ for any 𝓞_K[1/N]-order D₀ of D which is Azumaya over 𝓞_K[1/N] (N divisible by the ramified primes of D).

sources.match: Spreading out a Brauer class to an S-integral model.
Descent of finitely presented objects to a finite stage of a filtered colimit.

nodes.title: Azumaya algebras over the integers of a nonarchimedean local field are split
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, v a finite place, O_v = v.adicCompletionIntegers K with residue field κ_v (finite), and 𝒜₀ an Azumaya O_v-algebra. Then 𝒜₀ ≅ End_{O_v}(P) for a free O_v-module P of positive finite rank. Consequently K_v ⊗_{O_v} 𝒜₀ is a matrix algebra and its Brauer class in Br(K_v) is trivial.
hypotheses: O_v is a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field.
proofSteps: Residue algebra: κ_v ⊗ 𝒜₀ is Azumaya over the finite field κ_v (RP.2/azumaya-base-change), hence central simple, hence a matrix algebra M_n(κ_v), since Br(κ_v) is trivial (Tau Ceti subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite; Wedderburn).

Lifting an idempotent: 𝒜₀ is a finite free O_v-module, complete for the 𝔪_v-adic topology. A primitive idempotent ē of M_n(κ_v) of rank one lifts to an idempotent e ∈ 𝒜₀ (idempotents lift along the surjection 𝒜₀ → κ_v ⊗ 𝒜₀ with 𝔪-adically complete source: successive approximation e ↦ 3e² − 2e³).

P := 𝒜₀e is a direct summand of 𝒜₀, hence finite projective over the local ring O_v, hence free, of rank n since κ_v ⊗ P ≅ κ_v ⊗ 𝒜₀ ē ≅ κ_vⁿ. Left multiplication gives an O_v-algebra map 𝒜₀ → End_{O_v}(P) between free modules of rank n², which is an isomorphism modulo 𝔪_v (the matrix algebra acting on its column space), hence an isomorphism (Nakayama; a surjective endomorphism of a finite free module over a local ring with bijective reduction is bijective).
Base change to K_v gives End_{K_v}(K_v ⊗ P), whose class is 1 (Tau Ceti mk_end).

This is the Azumaya form of Poonen Corollary 6.9.3 (Br O_v = 0), which rests on Proposition 6.9.1 (Br of a complete local ring equals Br of its residue field), first proved for Azumaya algebras by Azumaya.
acceptance: For the Hamilton quaternions over ℤ_p with p odd, the lemma gives an isomorphism with M₂(ℤ_p); over ℤ₂ the standard order is not Azumaya, consistent with ℍ being ramified at 2.

nodes.title: Brauer evaluation is trivial at almost all places
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra, 𝒜 an Azumaya A-algebra and x ∈ X(𝔸_K) an adelic point (RP.2/adelic-points). Then 𝒜(x_v) = 1 in Br(K_v) for all but finitely many finite places v, where x_v is the local projection of x (RP.2/brauer-evaluation).
hypotheses: K a number field; A finitely generated; 𝒜 Azumaya over A.
proofSteps: Choose an integral model A₀ (RP.2/integral-model-exists-unique (a)) and spread 𝒜 out to an Azumaya A₀[1/N]-algebra 𝒜₀ (RP.2/azumaya-spreading-out).

By RP.2/adelic-points-restricted-product, x_v ∈ X₀(O_v) for all but finitely many v; discard also the finitely many v dividing N. For the remaining v, x_v restricts to an 𝓞_K-algebra map A₀[1/N] → O_v (N is a unit in O_v).
Then K_v ⊗_{A, x_v} 𝒜 ≅ K_v ⊗_{O_v} (O_v ⊗_{A₀[1/N]} 𝒜₀), and O_v ⊗ 𝒜₀ is Azumaya over O_v (RP.2/azumaya-base-change), hence split (RP.2/azumaya-complete-dvr-split); so 𝒜(x_v) = 1.
acceptance: For a constant algebra A ⊗_K D, the exceptional places are among the places where D ramifies, whatever the adelic point.
The finite set depends on x: for A = ℚ[t, 1/t] and 𝒜 = (−1, t)_A, a point with t = p at the place p gives the local class of (−1, p) over ℚ_p, which is nontrivial for p ≡ 3 mod 4.

nodes.title: The Brauer–Manin pairing and the Brauer–Manin set
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra. For each place v let inv_v : Br(K_v) → ℚ/ℤ be the local invariant (finite places: the invariant map of local class field theory, requested from ClassFieldTheory Layer 5; real places: Br(ℝ) ≅ ½ℤ/ℤ; complex places: 0). For an Azumaya A-algebra 𝒜 and x ∈ X(𝔸_K), the Brauer–Manin pairing is ⟨𝒜, x⟩ := Σ_v inv_v(𝒜(x_v)) ∈ ℚ/ℤ, a finite sum by RP.2/brauer-evaluation-finite-support (only finitely many terms are nonzero, and there are finitely many infinite places). The Brauer–Manin set of 𝒜 is X(𝔸_K)^𝒜 := {x : ⟨𝒜, x⟩ = 0}, and X(𝔸_K)^Br := ⋂_𝒜 X(𝔸_K)^𝒜 over all Azumaya A-algebras. There is a Brauer–Manin obstruction to the local-global principle for X if X(𝔸_K) ≠ ∅ and X(𝔸_K)^Br = ∅. Lean: `TauCeti.BrauerManin.pairing`, `brauerSet`, `brauerManinSet`, with ℚ/ℤ as AddCircle (1 : ℚ).
hypotheses: K a number field; A finitely generated; the local invariant maps are the requested ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 declarations (requests), used as given homomorphisms Br(K_v) → ℚ/ℤ. Br here is the Azumaya Brauer group of the affine scheme; the comparison with Poonen's cohomological Br X is recorded as a gap.
proofSteps: Finite support: RP.2/brauer-evaluation-finite-support at the finite places; the infinite places are finite in number.
The pairing is additive in 𝒜 (RP.2/brauer-evaluation (b) and additivity of each inv_v) and depends only on the Azumaya class; isomorphic algebras give the same sets.
X(𝔸_K)^𝒜 = X(𝔸_K) when 𝒜 is split (End_A(P)): every evaluation is 1.
acceptance: The Brauer–Manin set of the trivial algebra is all of X(𝔸_K).
If X(𝔸_K) = ∅ there is no Brauer–Manin obstruction in this sense: the definition requires adelic points.
A nonempty Brauer–Manin set does not by itself give a rational point (Poonen §8.6); the set is only an upper bound for the closure of X(K).

nodes.title: Rational points lie in the Brauer–Manin set
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra. For every K-point x ∈ X(K) and every Azumaya A-algebra 𝒜, ⟨𝒜, ι(x)⟩ = 0. Hence ι(X(K)) ⊆ X(𝔸_K)^Br, and a Brauer–Manin obstruction (X(𝔸_K) ≠ ∅, X(𝔸_K)^Br = ∅) implies X(K) = ∅.
hypotheses: As in RP.2/brauer-manin-pairing; the reciprocity law Σ_v inv_v(res_v β) = 0 for β ∈ Br(K) is the requested ClassFieldTheory Layer 10 theorem (requests).
proofSteps: For x ∈ X(K), the local projections of ι(x) are x followed by K → K_v, so by naturality (RP.2/brauer-evaluation (a)) 𝒜(ι(x)_v) = res_v(𝒜(x)) with 𝒜(x) ∈ Br(K).
Hence ⟨𝒜, ι(x)⟩ = Σ_v inv_v(res_v(𝒜(x))), which vanishes by the reciprocity law of the Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether sequence 0 → Br K → ⊕_v Br K_v → ℚ/ℤ → 0.
The inclusion in X(𝔸_K)^Br follows for all 𝒜 at once, and the obstruction statement is its contrapositive.
acceptance: For the constant algebra A ⊗ D of a central simple K-algebra D, the pairing vanishes on every adelic point whose local components come from K-points, and more generally ⟨A ⊗ D, x⟩ = Σ_v inv_v(D_v) = 0 for every adelic point (constant algebras give no obstruction).

nodes.title: Adelic points of separated schemes of finite type
nodes.statement: For a separated finite-type K-scheme X over a number field, choose a model 𝒳 over O_{K,S}. Define X(𝔸_K) as the union over finite T⊇S of Π_{v∈T}X(K_v)×Π_{v∉T}𝒳(O_v), equipped with the direct-limit topology. The topology is independent of the model and recovers the affine restricted product. Rational points map diagonally and morphisms induce continuous maps. For proper X the model is proper outside a finite set, and the adelic space is the product of all local spaces. A finite affine cover of X does not in general cover its adelic points: different places may require different charts. A global open immersion induces a continuous injection, generally not a topological embedding.
hypotheses: X separated of finite type over a number field K; places include the archimedean ones.
proofSteps: Conrad §3 gives the integral-model direct-limit construction and its model independence; compare with the affine case using finite presentation.
Extend each morphism to models after enlarging S. On every finite T-stage the induced map is continuous, hence continuous for the direct-limit topology.
For proper X, the valuative criterion identifies integral and local points outside S. Conrad §4, pp.9–10, shows why global affine-chart gluing and global open-immersion embeddings are invalid.
acceptance: For X = ℙ¹, X(𝔸_ℚ) = Π_v ℙ¹(ℚ_v), compact.
For X = 𝔾_m = Spec ℚ[t, 1/t], X(𝔸_ℚ) is the idele group with its idelic topology.

nodes.title: Evaluation of scheme Brauer classes at points
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme and α ∈ Br_Az(X) (SchemeAndStackFoundations key/scheme-brauer). For a field L and x ∈ X(L) put α(x) = x*α ∈ Br_Az(Spec L), identified with Mathlib's Brauer group of central simple L-algebras (Tau Ceti TauCeti.BrauerGroup). α(x) is a group homomorphism in α, natural in L, compatible with pullback along morphisms of schemes, and on affine X = Spec R it agrees with the evaluation of brauer-evaluation for Azumaya R-algebras. For x ∈ X(K_v) over a local field it lands in Br(K_v).

nodes.title: Local constancy of Brauer evaluation
nodes.statement: Let k be a local field and X a k-variety. For α ∈ Br X, the map X(k) → Br k, x ↦ α(x), is locally constant for the analytic topology on X(k). If k is nonarchimedean with ring of integers O, 𝒳 is a finite-type O-model and α extends to Br 𝒳, then x ↦ α(x) is constant on 𝒳(O) and equal to 0 when Br O = 0.
hypotheses: k a local field; X of finite type over k.
proofSteps: Near x the class extends over the henselisation of the local ring at the point; Brauer classes of henselian local rings are determined by the residue field (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2/brauer-henselian-local), and nearby points factor through a common henselian neighbourhood (Poonen Proposition 8.2.9 and its proof).
For O-points of a model: the class extends over Spec O, and Br O = 0 for complete discrete valuation rings with finite residue field (azumaya-complete-dvr-split).
acceptance: For the Brauer class (t,−1) on 𝔾_m,ℝ, the evaluation is constant on each sign component of ℝ× and the two values differ. The class is ramified at 0 and ∞, so it is not a class on ℙ¹_ℝ.

nodes.title: The Brauer–Manin pairing and set for varieties
nodes.statement: For a variety X over a number field K, the Brauer–Manin pairing X(𝔸_K) × Br X → ℚ/ℤ, ((x_v), α) ↦ Σ_v inv_v α(x_v), is well defined (α(x_v) = 0 for almost all v), additive in α, continuous and locally constant in (x_v) for each fixed α. For a subgroup B ⊆ Br X, X(𝔸_K)^B is the set of adelic points orthogonal to B, and X(𝔸_K)^{Br} = X(𝔸_K)^{Br X}. Rational points are orthogonal to Br X: X(K) ⊆ X(𝔸_K)^{Br}. There is a Brauer–Manin obstruction to the local-global principle when X(𝔸_K) ≠ ∅ but X(𝔸_K)^{Br} = ∅. On affine X with Azumaya classes this is brauer-manin-pairing.
hypotheses: K a number field; X separated of finite type over K; Br X is the Azumaya Brauer group of key/scheme-brauer.
inv_v is the local invariant of ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 (inv_∞ ∈ ½ℤ/ℤ at real places, 0 at complex places).
proofSteps: Finite support: spread X and α out to O_{K,S}; for v ∉ S, x_v ∈ 𝒳(O_v) and α(x_v) ∈ Br O_v = 0 (Poonen Proposition 8.2.1; brauer-evaluation-finite-support for the affine case).
Orthogonality of rational points: α(x) ∈ Br K and Σ_v inv_v = 0 (ClassFieldTheory Layer 10; Poonen Proposition 8.2.2, Corollary 8.2.6).
acceptance: For constant α = π*β, β ∈ Br K, the pairing is Σ_v inv_v β = 0 for every adelic point.

nodes.title: Topology of Brauer–Manin sets
nodes.statement: For X a variety over a number field K and B ⊆ Br X: X(𝔸)^B is closed in X(𝔸); for B finite (or finitely generated) it is open and closed; the closure of X(K) in X(𝔸) lies in X(𝔸)^{Br}. Hence for X proper, if X(𝔸)^{Br} ≠ X(𝔸) then X does not satisfy weak approximation.
hypotheses: K a number field.
proofSteps: Each α ↦ pairing is locally constant (brauer-local-constancy plus finite support), so X(𝔸)^{α} is open and closed; intersect over α ∈ B.
X(K) ⊆ X(𝔸)^{Br} and closedness give the closure statement (Poonen Corollary 8.2.11).

For a fixed α and an adelic point, spread α and choose an integral-model neighborhood on which all evaluations outside one finite S vanish uniformly. Pointwise finite support alone does not prove local constancy of the sum.
acceptance: The Iskovskikh surface has X(𝔸) ≠ ∅ = X(𝔸)^{Br}, so X(ℚ) = ∅.

nodes.title: Functoriality of Brauer–Manin sets
nodes.statement: For a morphism π : X' → X of K-varieties and B ⊆ Br X, π(X'(𝔸)^{π*B}) ⊆ X(𝔸)^B; in particular π(X'(𝔸)^{Br}) ⊆ X(𝔸)^{Br}, so X ↦ X(𝔸)^{Br} is functorial, and if X(𝔸)^{Br} = ∅ then X'(𝔸)^{Br} = ∅ for every X' mapping to X.
hypotheses: K a number field; π a morphism of finite-type separated K-schemes.
proofSteps: Naturality of evaluation: (π*α)(x') = α(π x') (scheme-brauer-evaluation), summed over places (Poonen Proposition 8.1.8 for the functor Br, Corollaries 8.1.9–8.1.10).
acceptance: Any variety mapping to the Iskovskikh surface has empty Brauer–Manin set.

nodes.title: Constant and algebraic Brauer groups
nodes.statement: For a variety X over a field k with separable closure k^s: Br₀(X) = image of Br k → Br X (the image, which need not be injective); Br₁(X) = ker(Br X → Br X_{k^s}); Br₀ ⊆ Br₁. If X is smooth geometrically integral with k^s[X]^× = k^{s×}, the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence gives an exact sequence Br k → Br₁ X → H¹(k, Pic X_{k^s}) → H³(k, 𝔾_m), so Br₁ X/Br₀ X ≅ H¹(k, Pic X_{k^s}) over number fields (H³(k, 𝔾_m) = 0). The Brauer–Manin pairing restricted to Br₀ is zero, so it factors through Br X/Br₀ X.
hypotheses: X a k-variety; Br is the Azumaya Brauer group of key/scheme-brauer (equal to the cohomological one for smooth quasi-projective X).

The Hochschild–Serre statement is naturally for the cohomological Brauer group. To identify it with the Azumaya group used here, assume the Gabber comparison hypotheses (in particular regular quasi-projective X over a field), or carry the comparison map explicitly.
proofSteps: Definitions are images and kernels of pullback maps (SF.2/pullback).
The exact sequence is SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2/brauer-hochschild-serre-sequence; H³(k, 𝔾_m) = 0 for number fields is ClassFieldTheory Layer 10.
acceptance: If X(k) ≠ ∅, Br k → Br X is injective (split by a point).

nodes.title: The unramified Brauer group
nodes.statement: For a smooth geometrically integral variety V over a field k of characteristic 0, Br_nr(V) is the image of Br(V^c) → Br(V) for a smooth proper compactification V ⊆ V^c; it does not depend on V^c and equals the subgroup of Br V of classes unramified at every discrete valuation of k(V) trivial on k. Br_{1,nr}(V) = Br_nr(V) ∩ Br₁(V). For V proper, Br_nr(V) = Br V.
hypotheses: char k = 0 (resolution of singularities provides V^c; purity for the Brauer group gives the valuation description).

The smooth-compactification proof is asserted here in characteristic zero. In positive characteristic, the all-valuations definition and appropriate purity statements require a separate proof and do not follow from resolution for curves.
proofSteps: Independence of V^c: two compactifications are dominated by a third and Br of smooth proper varieties is a birational invariant (purity; Česnavičius).
The valuative description: residues along divisors of V^c (SF.2 Brauer of regular schemes injects into Br k(V)).

Use the regular Brauer intersection theorem (Česnavičius Thm.1.2) for codimension-one points. Passing from a chosen model to all valuations and comparing arbitrary-dimensional compactifications requires its own purity/birational contract, recorded as unresolved.

nodes.title: The unramified pairing on the full product of local points
nodes.statement: For a smooth geometrically integral variety V over a number field K, the pairing Π_v V(K_v) × Br_nr(V) → ℚ/ℤ, ((x_v), α) ↦ Σ_v inv_v α(x_v), has finite support even on the full product (not only on V(𝔸_K)); it is additive in α, locally constant, and the diagonal image of V(K) is orthogonal to Br_nr(V).
hypotheses: V smooth geometrically integral over a number field K.
proofSteps: Extend α to a smooth proper compactification V^c and spread out over O_{K,S}; for v ∉ S, x_v ∈ V(K_v) ⊆ V^c(K_v) = 𝒱^c(O_v) and α(x_v) ∈ Br O_v = 0 (properness replaces integrality).
acceptance: Constant classes pair to 0 with every element of the product.

sources.match: Summing local invariants pairs Π_v V(k_v) with Br_nr(V); unramifiedness gives finite support on the full product.

nodes.title: Almost-everywhere locally trivial algebraic Brauer classes
nodes.statement: For a smooth geometrically integral variety V over a number field K, B_ω(V) ⊆ Br₁(V)/Br₀(V) is the subgroup of classes whose image in Br₁(V_{K_v})/Br₀(V_{K_v}) vanishes for all but finitely many places v. Under the Hochschild–Serre identification Br₁/Br₀ ≅ H¹(K, Pic V_{K̄}) these are the classes locally trivial at almost all places. At every place outside its finite exceptional set a class of B_ω evaluates constantly on V(K_v), so its pairing with V(𝔸_K) depends only on finitely many local components; classes trivial at every place (Ш¹(K, Pic V_{K̄})) pair constantly.
hypotheses: K a number field; k^s[V]^× = k^{s×} for the H¹ description.
proofSteps: Localisation maps on Br₁/Br₀ and on H¹(K, Pic V̄) commute with Hochschild–Serre; a class whose localisation lies in Br₀(V_{K_v}) evaluates constantly on V(K_v).
acceptance: Constant classes (zero in Br₁/Br₀) lie in B_ω.

nodes.title: The Brauer–Manin pairing on zero-cycles
nodes.statement: For a smooth proper variety X over a number field K and a closed point P of X_{K_v}, put α(P) = cor_{K_v(P)/K_v}(α restricted to P) ∈ Br K_v. Extending linearly gives ⟨,⟩ : Z₀(X_{𝔸}) × Br X → ℚ/ℤ, (Σ_v z_v, α) ↦ Σ_v inv_v α(z_v), on families of local zero-cycles (z_v)_v; it vanishes on principal divisors, on norms from ℂ at archimedean places, and on the diagonal image of global zero-cycles. For a rational point it is the ordinary pairing.
hypotheses: X smooth proper over a number field; zero-cycles of any degree.
proofSteps: Corestriction is compatible with local invariants (inv_v ∘ cor = inv_w; ClassFieldTheory Layer 5).
Rational equivalence: Weil reciprocity for Brauer classes on curves through the norm; global cycles pair to 0 by the reciprocity law for each finite extension K(P)/K.

The descent to rational equivalence requires Brauer reciprocity on curves, including specialization and corestriction for principal divisors. An intersection-number projection formula alone does not provide this theorem; its precise supplier is requested below.

nodes.title: Harari's formal lemma
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth proper rationally connected variety over a number field K, V ⊆ X a dense open subset and A ⊆ Br(V) a subgroup with A/(A ∩ Br X) finite. Then V(𝔸_K)^A is dense in X(𝔸_K)^{A ∩ Br X}.
hypotheses: The finiteness of the quotient A/(A ∩ Br X) (not of Br V) is the hypothesis used.
proofSteps: Colliot-Thélène–Skorobogatov 2000 Proposition 1.1 (as used by Harpaz–Wittenberg 2020, proof of Corollary 2.2): ramified classes can be compensated at auxiliary places by choosing local points near the boundary divisors.
acceptance: For A ⊆ Br X the statement is the density of V(𝔸)^A in X(𝔸)^A (V(K_v) is dense in X(K_v)).

nodes.title: Cyclic algebras and the local invariant matrix
nodes.statement: Let L/K be a cyclic extension of number fields of degree r with a character χ : Gal(K̄/K) → ℤ/r cutting out L. For a ∈ K_v^× the cyclic algebra (χ, a) has class in Br(K_v)[r], zero iff a is a norm from L ⊗ K_v. For polynomials P₁, …, P_n ∈ K[t] and local inputs t_v, the local invariant matrix is b_{v,i} = inv_v(χ, P_i(t_v)) ∈ (1/r)ℤ/ℤ.
hypotheses: L/K cyclic of degree r; χ a generator of the character group of Gal(L/K).
proofSteps: The cyclic algebra and its norm criterion over local fields are ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 inputs (local invariant of cyclic algebras); the matrix is a bookkeeping device recording these invariants.
acceptance: For K = ℚ, L = ℚ(i), r = 2: (χ, a)_p = (−1, a)_p, the Hilbert symbol.

nodes.title: The cyclic norm principle with one omitted place
nodes.statement: Let L/K be cyclic and a ∈ K^×. If a is a local norm from L at every place except possibly one, then a is a norm from L^×.
hypotheses: L/K cyclic (essential).
proofSteps: All local invariants of (χ, a) but one vanish; the sum of invariants is 0 (ClassFieldTheory Layer 10), so all vanish; the Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether injectivity gives (χ, a) = 0, and the cyclic splitting criterion (cyclicHasseNorm of ClassFieldTheory Layer 13) makes a a global norm.
acceptance: For L = ℚ(i): if a is a sum of two squares in ℚ_p for every p ≠ 3 and in ℝ, it is a sum of two rational squares.

sources.locator: proof of Theorem 5.3, p. 720, citing Colliot-Thélène–Skorobogatov, The Brauer–Grothendieck group, Corollary 13.1.10
sources.match: A local norm everywhere but one place is a global norm for cyclic extensions.

nodes.title: Assembling a global norm from a local invariant matrix
nodes.statement: In the cyclic-norm setting, choose nonzero q_i=P_i(ν) with distinct designated exceptional places outside S. Write b_{v,i}=inv_v(χ,q_i) at v∈S. Require both Σ_{v∈S}b_{v,i}=0 for every i and Σ_i b_{v,i}=0 for every v∈S, together with vanishing outside S and each designated exceptional place, including at archimedean places. Reciprocity kills the invariant at the exceptional place separately for each i. The placewise sums then show that the product Π_i q_i has trivial cyclic-algebra class everywhere, hence is a global norm. Neither of the two sum conditions may be omitted.
hypotheses: L/K cyclic; the terms q_i are treated separately (no repeated-prime obstruction).
proofSteps: Use the first condition, the fixed-i sum over S, in the reciprocity formula for each cyclic algebra (χ,q_i) to kill its single remaining local invariant.
Use the second condition, the fixed-place sum over i, for the product at S. Additivity gives zero at every other place; apply the cyclic Hasse norm theorem.
acceptance: With n = 1 this is cyclic-norm-one-place for a = q₁.

sources.match: The local-to-global assembly of a product norm from the invariant matrix and the reciprocity law.

nodes.title: Brauer groups of high-dimensional complete intersections
nodes.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic 0 and X ⊆ ℙⁿ_k a smooth complete intersection with dim X ≥ 3. Then Br k → Br X is an isomorphism. Consequently, over a number field, X(𝔸_K)^{Br} = X(𝔸_K) (and X(𝔸)^{descent} = X(𝔸)): the Brauer–Manin and descent obstructions are vacuous. This does not prove that X has a rational point.
hypotheses: char k = 0; dim X ≥ 3; X a smooth complete intersection.
proofSteps: Use Lefschetz to identify Pic X_{k̄}=ℤ·O(1) and H²(X_{k̄},μ_n) with the corresponding projective-space group for every n. The Kummer sequence then gives Br X_{k̄}[n]=0; torsion gives Br X_{k̄}=0. The hyperplane bundle descends, H¹(k,ℤ)=0, and Hochschild–Serre gives Br X=Br₀ X. H³(k,𝔾_m)=0 is the number-field spectral-sequence input, not a substitute for the geometric H²/Kummer calculation.
Vacuity: constant classes pair trivially (brauer-manin-general); descent: X_{k̄} is algebraically simply connected and Theorem 8.5.4 (RP.3/etale-brauer-equals-descent).
acceptance: Smooth cubic threefolds and quartic threefolds in ℙ⁴ have no Brauer–Manin obstruction.

sources.locator: §8.6.3, Theorem 8.6.12 and sketch of proof, p. 252
sources.match: For smooth complete intersections of dimension ≥ 3 over a number field the descent and Brauer–Manin obstructions are vacuous; (ii) Br k → Br X is an isomorphism, citing Poonen–Voloch Proposition A.1.
Uses that the Brauer–Manin obstruction is vacuous for high-dimensional complete intersections, as motivation for the Hasse principle for random Fano hypersurfaces.

nodes.title: Conics: Brauer–Manin set and the Hasse principle
nodes.statement: Let C ⊆ ℙ²_K be a smooth conic over a number field K. Then Br C = Br₀ C, so C(𝔸_K)^{Br} = C(𝔸_K); C satisfies the Hasse principle (C(𝔸_K) ≠ ∅ ⇒ C(K) ≠ ∅) and weak approximation once C(K) ≠ ∅. For C : x² + y² = 3z² over ℚ, C(ℚ₃) = ∅, so C(𝔸_ℚ) = ∅.
hypotheses: C smooth projective conic over a number field.
proofSteps: C_{K̄} ≅ ℙ¹, so Pic C_{K̄} = ℤ with trivial Galois action and H¹(K, ℤ) = 0: Br₁ = Br₀ and Br C_{K̄} = 0.
Hasse principle: Hasse–Minkowski for ternary forms (TauCetiRoadmap GlobalQuadraticForms Layer 5).
acceptance: x² + y² = 3z² has no ℚ₃-point (sums of two squares are not 3 times a unit square modulo 9 with the valuation count).

sources.locator: §4.5, Theorem 4.5.11 (Châtelet: Severi–Brauer varieties satisfy the local-global principle), p. 108
sources.match: Conics are one-dimensional Severi–Brauer varieties and satisfy the Hasse principle over global fields.

nodes.title: Iskovskikh's conic bundle surface
nodes.statement: Let X be the smooth proper model of the affine surface y² + z² = (3 − x²)(x² − 2) over ℚ (a Châtelet surface). Then X(𝔸_ℚ) ≠ ∅ but X(𝔸_ℚ)^{𝒜} = ∅ for the quaternion class 𝒜 = (3 − x², −1) ∈ Br X; hence X(ℚ) = ∅ and the failure of the Hasse principle is explained by the Brauer–Manin obstruction.
hypotheses: The class 𝒜 extends from the function field to Br X (Poonen Proposition 8.2.14).
proofSteps: Local solubility by Hensel's lemma at every p and at ∞.

Local invariants: inv_p 𝒜(P) = 0 for p ∉ {2, ∞} (units, Br ℤ_p = 0); inv_∞ 𝒜(P) = 0 for every real point (3 − x² or x² − 2 is positive, a norm from ℂ); inv_2 𝒜(P) = 1/2 for every P ∈ X(ℚ₂) (the relevant function is ≡ −1 mod 4, not a sum of two 2-adic squares); the sum is 1/2 ≠ 0 (Poonen Proposition 8.2.15).
acceptance: The pairing of 𝒜 with every adelic point is 1/2.

sources.locator: §8.2.5, Proposition 8.2.14 and Proposition 8.2.15 with proof, pp. 232–235
sources.match: Iskovskikh's Châtelet surface has adelic points but empty Brauer set, so no rational points.

nodes.title: Finite local partitions for a finite Brauer test; effective computation requires extra input
nodes.statement: For a proper variety X over a number field and a finite list of Brauer classes, there is a finite set T of places and, at each v∈T, a finite partition of the compact space X(K_v) by clopen evaluation fibres. The orthogonality condition is therefore a finite constraint on these fibres. This is an existence theorem: local constancy and compactness alone do not compute T, the nonempty fibres, or a terminating local solver. An effective algorithm additionally needs certified spreading data, local solution enumeration and explicit evaluation formulae. The Iskovskikh example supplies those extra data in that particular case.
hypotheses: X smooth proper; B finite and given explicitly; the local invariants of ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 computed on explicit algebras.
proofSteps: Spread the fixed finite list of classes over one integral model so that evaluation vanishes outside a common finite T.

For each v∈T use local constancy and compactness to obtain finitely many evaluation fibres; at archimedean places use the finite connected-component description. This proves a finite partition, not an algorithm.
acceptance: For the Iskovskikh surface, T = {2, ∞} and the computation is Proposition 8.2.15.

sources.match: For proper X the pairing with a Brauer class admits a finite explicit description: locally constant functions factor through finite levels and almost all places contribute 0; effectivity of searching for obstructing algebras.

nodes.title: Evaluation of torsors and twisted torsors
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, X a k-variety, G a smooth affine algebraic group over k and f : Z → X a G-torsor with class ζ ∈ H¹_fppf(X, G). For x ∈ X(L), ζ(x) ∈ H¹(L, G) is the class of the fibre Z_x. For a cocycle class τ ∈ H¹(k, G) represented by a torsor T, the twisted torsor f^τ : Z^τ = Z ×^G T^{-1} → X is a torsor under the inner form G_τ. Evaluation is natural in L and in X, and commutes with twisting: ζ^τ(x) corresponds to ζ(x) under the twisting bijection H¹(k, G) ≅ H¹(k, G_τ). The twisting bijection sends τ to the trivial class. For commutative G, [Z^τ]=[Z]−π*τ; x lifts to Z^τ exactly when ζ(x)=res(τ).
hypotheses: G smooth affine (for twisting by the contracted product); H¹ is fppf (equal to Galois cohomology for smooth G over a field).
proofSteps: Pullback of torsors along x : Spec L → X (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1/torsor-cohomology).
Twisting: contracted product with T^{-1} (SF.1/contracted-product, SF.1/twisting-bijection; Poonen Example 6.5.12).
acceptance: For the torsor [2] : A → A under A[2], evaluation at a ∈ A(k) is the Kummer class δ(a) (RP.1/kummer-map).

sources.locator: §8.4.1, evaluation of a torsor at rational points, pp. 239–240; §6.5, Example 6.5.12 (twisted torsor), p. 183
sources.match: A G-torsor over X gives an evaluation map X(k) → H¹(k, G); twisting by τ gives Z^τ → X under the inner form.

nodes.title: The descent partition of rational points
nodes.statement: In the setting of torsor-evaluation, {x ∈ X(k) : ζ(x) = τ} = f^τ(Z^τ(k)) for every τ ∈ H¹(k, G); hence X(k) is the disjoint union over τ ∈ H¹(k, G) of f^τ(Z^τ(k)).
hypotheses: G smooth affine; X a k-variety.
proofSteps: x ∈ f^τ(Z^τ(k)) iff the fibre of Z^τ at x is trivial iff Z_x ≅ T as G-torsors iff ζ(x) = τ (Poonen Theorem 8.4.1 and its proof, using Proposition 5.12.14).
acceptance: For y² = (x² + 1)(x⁴ + 1) and the μ₂-torsors Z_c given by c w² = x⁴ + 1, X(ℚ) = ⋃_c f_c(Z_c(ℚ)) (Poonen §8.3).

sources.match: Rational points with a given fibre class are exactly images of rational points of the corresponding twist; X(k) is the disjoint union over H¹(k, G).

nodes.title: The Selmer set of a torsor
nodes.statement: For a global field k and a G-torsor f : Z → X, Sel_Z(k, G) = {τ ∈ H¹(k, G) : τ_v ∈ image of X(k_v) → H¹(k_v, G) for all places v} = {τ : Z^τ(k_v) ≠ ∅ for all v}. Then X(k) = ⨆_{τ ∈ Sel_Z(k,G)} f^τ(Z^τ(k)). If X is proper, Sel_Z(k, G) is finite, and there is a finite separable extension k'/k with X(k) ⊆ f(Z(k')).
hypotheses: k a global field; finiteness needs X proper.

For the trivial-torsor identification with Ш¹(k,G), assume X(𝔸_k)≠∅. For global function fields use the global-field adelic and finite-cohomology contracts, not merely the number-field constructions of RP.2.
proofSteps: Spread X, Z, G out over O_{k,S}; for v ∉ S local images come from H¹(O_v, G) (valuative criterion); for v ∈ S the local images of the finite component group are finite (local-evaluation-finite-image); H¹_S(k, G) has finite fibres over finitely many local data (Poonen Theorem 6.5.13).
The extension k': each τ in the finite Selmer set dies over some finite separable extension; take a compositum (Poonen Corollary 8.4.8).
acceptance: For f = [2] : E → E on an elliptic curve over a number field, Sel_Z(k, E[2]) is the 2-Selmer group (Poonen Remark 8.4.5).

nodes.title: Finite local images of torsor evaluation
nodes.statement: Let k be a local field, X a proper k-variety, F a finite étale algebraic group over k and f : Z → X an F-torsor. Then the image of X(k) → H¹(k, F) is finite; if char k = 0, H¹(k, F) itself is finite.
hypotheses: k local; X proper; F finite étale.
proofSteps: Krasner's lemma makes the fibre class locally constant (the evaluation is continuous for the discrete topology on H¹); X(k) is compact for proper X (Poonen Proposition 8.4.2).
In characteristic 0, H¹(k, F) is finite (Poonen Theorem 5.12.24(a)).
acceptance: For X = ℙ¹ over ℚ_p and any F-torsor, the image is finite.

sources.match: The image of X(k) → H¹(k, F) is finite for proper X over a local field.

nodes.title: Descent obstruction sets
nodes.statement: Let k be a number field and X a k-variety. For a G-torsor f : Z → X under a smooth affine G, X(𝔸)^f is the set of adelic points whose image in Π_v H¹(k_v, G) comes from H¹(k, G); equivalently X(𝔸)^f = ⋃_{τ∈H¹(k,G)} f^τ(Z^τ(𝔸)) = ⋃_{τ∈Sel} f^τ(Z^τ(𝔸)), closed when X is proper. X(𝔸)^{H¹(X,G)} = ⋂_f X(𝔸)^f, X(𝔸)^{descent} = ⋂_G X(𝔸)^{H¹(X,G)} over all smooth affine G, and X(𝔸)^{ét}, X(𝔸)^{conn}, X(𝔸)^{PGL} restrict G to finite étale, smooth connected affine, PGL_n. Then X(k) ⊆ X(𝔸)^{descent} ⊆ X(𝔸). There is a descent obstruction when X(𝔸) ≠ ∅ = X(𝔸)^{descent}.
hypotheses: k a number field; G smooth affine; X separated of finite type.

For function fields the assertion requires the analogous adelic-space construction for global fields. RP.2 currently provides its number-field specialization; the extension is recorded as a gap rather than silently supplied by it.
proofSteps: Commutativity of X(k) → X(𝔸) with H¹(k, G) → Π_v H¹(k_v, G) (Poonen (8.4.13)) gives X(k) ⊆ X(𝔸)^f.
The union description and closedness for proper X: Poonen Exercise 8.7, via selmer-set-of-torsor and local-evaluation-finite-image.
acceptance: For the trivial torsor Z = X × G, X(𝔸)^f = X(𝔸).

sources.locator: §8.4.7, display (8.4.13), Definition 8.4.14 and the definitions of X(𝔸)^{ét}, X(𝔸)^{conn}, X(𝔸)^{PGL}, pp. 244–245
sources.match: Descent sets of torsors, their intersections over all torsors and groups, and the descent obstruction.

uses.how: adelic points orthogonal to f*^{-1}Br_nr(Y) lie in ⋃_σ f^σ(Y^σ(𝔸)^{Br_nr})

nodes.title: Descent is at least as strong as Brauer–Manin
nodes.statement: Let k be a number field and X a variety. For a PGL_n-torsor f : Z → X with Brauer class 𝒜 ∈ Br X[n], X(𝔸)^f = X(𝔸)^𝒜. If X is regular and quasi-projective, every class of Br X comes from some PGL_n-torsor, so X(𝔸)^{descent} ⊆ X(𝔸)^{PGL} = X(𝔸)^{Br}.
hypotheses: k a number field; for the equality X(𝔸)^{PGL} = X(𝔸)^{Br}, X regular quasi-projective (Gabber–de Jong: Br X = Br' X).
PGL_n-torsors classify Azumaya Brauer classes. Passage to the full cohomological Brauer group uses the regular quasi-projective Gabber comparison. Period=index is used only over number fields here.
proofSteps: The map H¹(X, PGL_n) → Br X[n] is compatible with evaluation; H¹(k, PGL_n) ≅ Br(k)[n] and H¹(k_v, PGL_n) ≅ Br(k_v)[n] (Poonen Remark 1.5.18), so the descent condition becomes the reciprocity condition (Poonen Lemma 8.5.2).
Every class of Br X is represented by an Azumaya algebra for X regular quasi-projective (Poonen Corollary 6.6.19; requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2).
acceptance: For the Iskovskikh surface the PGL₂-torsor of the quaternion algebra already obstructs.

sources.locator: §8.5.1, Lemma 8.5.2 and Proposition 8.5.3 with proofs, pp. 245–246
sources.match: The descent set of a PGL_n-torsor equals the Brauer set of its class; descent sets are contained in the Brauer–Manin set for regular quasi-projective X.

nodes.title: The étale–Brauer set
nodes.statement: For a variety X over a number field k, X(𝔸)^{ét,Br} = ⋂_{F finite étale} ⋂_{f : Z → X F-torsor} ⋃_{τ ∈ H¹(k,F)} f^τ(Z^τ(𝔸)^{Br}), and X(𝔸)^{ét,descent} is defined with Z^τ(𝔸)^{descent} in place of Z^τ(𝔸)^{Br}. Then X(k) ⊆ X(𝔸)^{ét,descent} ⊆ X(𝔸)^{ét,Br} ⊆ X(𝔸)^{Br}.
hypotheses: k a number field; X a variety.
proofSteps: Rational points: each x ∈ X(k) lifts to some Z^τ(k) (descent-partition), which lies in Z^τ(𝔸)^{Br} (RP.2/brauer-manin-general).
Inclusions from descent-brauer-comparison applied to the covers Z^τ and from the trivial torsor.
acceptance: For X with trivial étale fundamental group of X_{k̄} (for example ℙⁿ or a smooth complete intersection of dimension ≥ 2), X(𝔸)^{ét,Br} = X(𝔸)^{Br}.

sources.locator: §8.5.2, definitions of X(𝔸)^{ét,Br} and X(𝔸)^{ét,descent}, pp. 246–247
sources.match: The Brauer–Manin obstruction applied to all finite étale torsors and their twists.

nodes.title: Étale–Brauer equals descent
nodes.statement: For a smooth projective geometrically integral variety X over a number field k: X(𝔸)^{ét,Br} = X(𝔸)^{ét,descent} = X(𝔸)^{descent}. Moreover the descent obstruction is stable under iteration: X(𝔸)^{descent,descent} = X(𝔸)^{descent} for smooth quasi-projective geometrically integral X (Cao).
hypotheses: X nice (smooth, projective, geometrically integral) for the first equality; smooth quasi-projective geometrically integral for Cao's theorem.
proofSteps: X(𝔸)^{descent} ⊆ X(𝔸)^{ét,descent}: Skorobogatov 2009 Theorem 1.1 (a torsor under a smooth affine group over a finite étale cover is dominated by a torsor under a larger group over X).
X(𝔸)^{ét,descent} ⊆ X(𝔸)^{ét,Br}: descent-brauer-comparison on each cover.
X(𝔸)^{ét,Br} ⊆ X(𝔸)^{descent}: Demarche 2009, extending Harari's X(𝔸)^{conn} = X(𝔸)^{Br}.
Iteration: Cao 2017 Corollaire 1.2 and induction (Poonen Corollary 8.5.6).
acceptance: For Skorobogatov's bielliptic surface the empty étale–Brauer set is also explained by a single torsor under a noncommutative finite étale group (Poonen Remark 8.6.4).

sources.locator: §8.5.3, Theorem 8.5.4 and sketch of proof, p. 247; §8.5.4, Theorem 8.5.5 and Corollary 8.5.6, p. 248
sources.match: The étale–Brauer set equals the descent set for nice varieties over number fields (Demarche, Harari, Skorobogatov, Stoll); Cao's stability of descent under iteration.

nodes.title: Universal torsors and torsors of a given type
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth geometrically integral variety over a field k with k̄[X]^× = k̄^× and Pic X_{k̄} free of finite rank, and T the k-torus with character module T̂ = Pic X_{k̄}. A torsor f : Y → X under a k-torus T' has a type λ : T̂' → Pic X_{k̄}, the map sending a character to the class of the pushed-out 𝔾_m-torsor. A universal torsor is a T-torsor of type the identity. Universal torsors exist iff the type obstruction δ(id)∈H²(k,T) vanishes; they exist when X(k) ≠ ∅; any two differ by twisting by H¹(k, T).
hypotheses: X smooth geometrically integral with only constant invertible functions geometrically and Pic X_{k̄} free of finite rank (Colliot-Thélène–Sansuc).
proofSteps: Type map: the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for H¹(X, T') gives H¹(k, T') → H¹(X, T') → Hom_k(T̂', Pic X_{k̄}) → H²(k, T') (Colliot-Thélène–Sansuc); the type of a torsor is its image.
Twisting acts simply transitively on torsors of a fixed type (torsor-evaluation).

Here δ is the connecting map in the stated type exact sequence and id:T̂→Pic X_{k̄} defines the universal type. The existence assertion is δ(id)=0. No undefined Ext-valued elementary-obstruction carrier is introduced; comparison with that obstruction is a separate theorem.
acceptance: For X = ℙⁿ, Pic X_{k̄} = ℤ, T = 𝔾_m and the universal torsor is 𝔸^{n+1} ∖ {0} → ℙⁿ.

sources.locator: §2, p. 8; §6, proofs of Théorèmes 6.1 and 6.6; §7, Proposition 7.8
sources.match: Torsors under tori over X, their types, and universal torsors in the arguments of the paper.

nodes.title: Descent under tori and the algebraic Brauer group
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth geometrically integral over a number field k with k̄[X]^× = k̄^× and Pic X_{k̄} free of finite rank. If X is moreover proper, every adelic point orthogonal to Br₁ X lifts to the adelic points of some universal torsor: X(𝔸)^{Br₁} = ⋃_{Y universal} f_Y(Y(𝔸)). More generally, for a torsor f : Y → X under a torus T and A ⊇ the cup products H¹(k, T̂) ∪ [f] in Br X, every point of X(𝔸)^A lifts to Y^σ(𝔸) for some σ.
hypotheses: X smooth geometrically integral over a number field; the hypotheses on units and Pic for the universal-torsor statement.
proofSteps: Classical descent (Colliot-Thélène–Sansuc; Harari–Skorobogatov 2013 Theorem 8.4 and Proposition 8.12): the obstruction to lifting (x_v) is an element of Ш²(k, T) paired with x_v through the cup products, killed by orthogonality to H¹(k, T̂) ∪ [f] via Poitou–Tate for tori (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4/torus-sha-duality).
Harpaz–Wittenberg 2020 Proposition 2.5 states the case used there.
acceptance: For X = ℙⁿ both sides are X(𝔸).

sources.locator: Proposition 2.5 and proof, p. 10, citing Harari–Skorobogatov 2013 Theorem 8.4 and Proposition 8.12
sources.match: Every adelic point orthogonal to A lifts to some twist Y^σ(𝔸); the cup products H¹(k, T̂) ∪ [f] lie in ker f* ⊆ A.

nodes.title: The relative algebraic Brauer group of a torus torsor
nodes.statement: For a morphism f : Y → X of k-varieties, Br₁(Y/X) is the subgroup of Br Y of classes whose image in Br Y_{k̄} lies in the image of Br X_{k̄} → Br Y_{k̄}. For f a torsor under a k-torus T and Y smooth, Br_nr(Y) ⊆ Br₁(Y/X), since Y_{k̄} is birationally X_{k̄} × T_{k̄}. Under the hypotheses of Harpaz–Wittenberg §2 there is an exact sequence Br X → Br₁(Y^σ/X) --φ_σ--> H²(k, T̂) --δ_σ--> H³(X, 𝔾_m) from the Leray and Hochschild–Serre spectral sequences; pullbacks from Br X are killed by φ_σ, and the last group is H³(X, 𝔾_m) (not H³(k, 𝔾_m)).
hypotheses: f : Y → X a torsor under a k-torus T; Y, X smooth geometrically integral; k of characteristic 0.
proofSteps: Membership is an image condition, not a quotient equality.
Br_nr(Y) ⊆ Br₁(Y/X): unramified classes on X_{k̄} × T_{k̄} come from X_{k̄} (Br_nr of a torus over k̄ is 0).
The edge sequence: Leray for f and Hochschild–Serre for k̄/k (Harpaz–Wittenberg 2020 (2.2)).
acceptance: For Y = X × T (trivial torsor), Br₁(Y/X) ⊇ pr₁*Br X + pr₂*Br₁ T.

sources.match: Defines Br₁(Y/X), shows Br_nr(Y) ⊆ Br₁(Y/X) for torus torsors, and gives the relative Brauer edge sequence.

nodes.title: Twist independence of the relative Brauer edge maps
nodes.statement: In the setting of relative-algebraic-brauer, with σ ranging over H¹(k, T): (i) if H³(k, 𝔾_m) = 0 the map δ_σ : H²(k, T̂) → H³(X, 𝔾_m) does not depend on σ; (ii) if H³(k, 𝔾_m) = 0, the subgroup φ_σ(Br_nr(Y^σ)) ⊆ H²(k, T̂) does not depend on σ; (iii) without that hypothesis, f_σ*^{-1}(Br_nr(Y^σ)) ⊆ Br X does not depend on σ; (iv) for every extension L/k, α ∈ Br₁(Y^σ/X), y ∈ Y^σ(L) and t ∈ T(L), α(t·y) = α(y) + φ_σ(α) ∪ t in Br L (character evaluation pairing). For a torus torsor Z over k, Br₁(Z) = H²(k, k̄[Z]^×) with edge map to H²(k, T̂), onto when H³(k, 𝔾_m) = 0, and α(t·z) − α(z) = φ(α) ∪ t.
hypotheses: H³(k, 𝔾_m) = 0 in (i)–(ii), true for number fields and their completions.
proofSteps: δ_σ is the cup product with the class of f_σ up to a fixed sign; the difference for two twists factors through H³(k, 𝔾_m) (Harpaz–Wittenberg Proposition 2.3(i)).
(ii)–(iii) from (i) and the birational description of Br_nr; (iv) from Lemma 2.4 applied to the fibre torsor over L.
acceptance: For T = 𝔾_m and a 𝔾_m-torsor over Spec k, α(t·z) − α(z) = (χ, t) for the character class χ = φ(α).

sources.locator: §2, Lemma 2.4 and its proof, author-copy p.10
sources.match: Twist independence of δ_σ, of the unramified edge image and of pulled-back unramified classes; the translation formula for evaluation; the torus torsor over a field.

nodes.title: The residual Tate–Shafarevich functional
nodes.statement: In the setting of Harpaz–Wittenberg Theorem 2.1 (k a number field, f : Y → X a T-torsor, (x_v) ∈ X(𝔸)^A), choose an adelic lift y = (y_v) ∈ Y(𝔸) and identify the common edge image. For τ ∈ Ш¹(k, T) define ε_τ on Ш²(k, T̂) ∩ φ₀(Br_nr(Y)) by ε_τ(a) = Σ_v inv_v α_τ(y_v^τ) for any α_τ ∈ Br_nr(Y^τ) with φ_τ(α_τ) = a. The value does not depend on the choices, ε is additive, and ε_τ(a) = ε₀(a) + ⟨a, τ⟩ for the Poitou–Tate pairing ⟨,⟩ : Ш²(k, T̂) × Ш¹(k, T) → ℚ/ℤ. Here A=(f*)⁻¹Br_nr(Y) is the precise orthogonality subgroup. With Poonen’s twist parameter τ, HW’s parameter is σ=−τ; hence ε_τ(a)=ε₀(a)+⟨a,τ⟩.
hypotheses: k a number field; twist and Poitou–Tate sign conventions as fixed in torsor-evaluation and ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4/torus-sha-duality.
proofSteps: Independence of α_τ: two choices differ by a pullback from Br X, which pairs to 0 with x_v ∈ X(𝔸)^A.
Independence of y: changing y_v by t_v ∈ T(k_v) changes the sum by Σ_v inv_v(a ∪ t_v) = 0 since a is locally trivial (edge-map-twist-independence (iv)).
Variation: compare the twists by σ through (iv) and the definition of the Poitou–Tate pairing (Harpaz–Wittenberg Proposition 2.6).
acceptance: If Ш²(k, T̂) = 0 (for example T split), ε is the zero functional on the zero group.

sources.locator: §2, unnumbered definition of ε and its variation formula, author-copy pp.10–11
sources.match: Definition and well-definedness of the residual functional ε_τ and its variation ε_τ = ε₀ − ⟨·, σ⟩.
